name: Dharmalinga Malai
deity: Shiva (Dharmalingeswarar), worshipped as a swayambhu lingam
significance: A hilltop Shiva shrine about 13 km south of Coimbatore, reached by a climb of nearly 800 steps. Its Chitra Pournami girivalam draws crowds in the tens of thousands.

name: ISKCON Temple, Pune
style: North Indian (red stone and marble), with a South Indian Venkateswara shrine
significance: A six-acre Gaudiya Vaishnava temple complex in Kondhwa built over seven years and inaugurated in 2013, described as the largest temple in Pune. It runs daily Bhagavad Gita and Srimad Bhagavatam classes.

name: Shri Alkheswar Mahadev Mandir
significance: A Shiva temple in Bera village, Mathura district, whose walled complex also holds shrines to Ram and Sita, Ganesha, Brahma, Durga, Radha Krishna, Shani and Hanuman beside a sacred tank. A fair is held each March and Mahashivratri draws the largest crowds.
story: The Shiva idol of the main shrine is said to have been found in the Alkheswar Kund, the pond adjoining the temple.

name: Somabaresvara Siva Temple
deity: Shiva (lingam set in a square sandstone yonipitha)
significance: A small west-facing Shiva shrine inside the Kapilesvara temple precinct at Bhubaneswar, now buried up to its baranda. Its tiered pidha superstructure is a compact example of Kalinga temple form.

name: Siddheshwar & Ratneshwar Temple
significance: A paired Shaiva temple about 2 km from Latur city, credited to the reign of King Tamradwaj. It hosts a large annual fair at Mahashivratri.

name: Bhawani Waghjai Temple, Terav
deity: Bhavani and Waghjai, with Kalkai, Navdurga and Shiva
significance: A goddess temple at Terav in Chiplun taluka, rebuilt from May 2003 on a shrine of the nineteenth century. The 123 ft hall seats about 2,000 people beneath a 55 ft dome over a 9 ft black-stone Bhavani image.

name: Sarasbaug Ganpati Temple
significance: Built in 1784 by Sawai Madhavrao Peshwa on an island in the lake laid out below Parvati Hill, this Ganesha temple is one of Pune's busiest shrines, with roughly 10,000 visitors a day rising to 80,000 at Ganesh Chaturthi.

name: Shri Katyayani Baneshwar Temple, Aversa
significance: A coastal Karnataka temple of about 1600 whose goddess is the kuladevi of Konkani Gaud Saraswat, Saraswat and Daivajnya Brahmin families and of Konkani Kharvis. Its trust now runs the temple on solar power.

name: Kundrathur Murugan Temple
significance: A hill temple on the outskirts of Chennai attributed to Kulothunga Chola II, and said to be the only Murugan shrine in Tamil Nadu where the god faces north. It is administered by the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department.
story: Murugan is said to have halted on this hill while travelling from Tiruporur to Tiruttani after defeating the demons, which is why the site is called South Thanigai.

name: Camp Hanuman Temple
significance: One of India's largest Hanuman temples, founded by Pandit Gajanan Prasad inside the Ahmedabad cantonment and long associated with army personnel. A 2021 proposal by its trustees to move it to the Sabarmati riverfront was blocked after priests and devotees petitioned the Gujarat High Court.
story: The Hanuman image enshrined here is held to be swayambhu, self-manifested rather than carved.

name: Sasthamcotta Sree Dharma Sastha Temple
deity: Dharma Sastha, with consort Prabha and son Sathyaka
significance: One of the five ancient Sastha temples of Kerala, alongside Sabarimala, Achankovil, Aryankavu and Kulathupuzha, standing on high ground ringed on three sides by the state's largest freshwater lake. Its resident monkeys are treated as sacred and are cared for by a trust fund set up in 1996.
story: Rama is said to have stopped here on his return from Lanka to honour Dharma Sastha, leaving behind Neelan, chief architect of his vanara army, whose descendants are held to be the temple's monkeys.

name: Sikharagiriswara Temple, Kudumiyamalai
significance: A rock temple at Kudumiyanmalai near Pudukkottai carrying inscriptions of the Pallava king Mahendravarman, among them a celebrated treatise on music. Its later complex includes a thousand-pillared hall and mandapas carved as chariots drawn by elephants and horses.

name: Shri Mansa Mata Mandir, Hasampur
significance: A Shakta temple set in a hundred-acre complex in the Hasampur hills near Neem-Ka-Thana, counted among the prominent goddess shrines of north India and thronged during Navratri. It is run by the Shri Mata Mansa Devi Shrine Board constituted under a 1991 Rajasthan act.

name: Shani Dham Temple
significance: A Delhi temple to Shani at Asola, reported to hold the largest rock image of the deity in the world, unveiled on 31 May 2003. Its eastern hall sets the Shani image beside the twelve Jyotirlingas, while the western section adds Shani on buffalo and vulture, Hanuman, an oblation pool and the nine planets.

name: Shree Vishnumurthy Temple
builtDisplay: idol c. 600 years old; shrine rebuilt after 1911
significance: An old Vishnu shrine at Kulai north of Mangalore, found in ruins in the forest around 1911 by the local historian Venkatramana Hebbar and repeatedly renovated since. Its image is reckoned to be about six centuries old.

name: Siddha Vinayaka Temple
significance: A Ganapatya shrine in Ganjam district built around an idol that still sits within the joined trunks of two ficus trees, counted in Odisha's Panchadevata tradition. Around 200,000 pilgrims from Odisha and Andhra Pradesh come for Ganesh Chaturthi.
story: The Gajapati king Purushottama Deva of Puri is said to have found the idol in the hollow of a banyan and a peepal while marching on the Kanchi kingdom, and to have consecrated it on the spot.

name: Siddhivinayak Mahaganapati Temple, Titwala
significance: A much-visited Ganesha temple at Titwala on an ancient site, renovated under Peshwa Madhavrao I and rebuilt in 1965-66, with further work finished in 2009. Devotees come specifically to seek marriages and to settle marital difficulties.
story: Sage Kanva is said to have told Shakuntala, estranged from King Dushyanta, to raise a shrine here to Ganesha as Siddhi Vinayaka.

name: Sita Samahit Sthal
significance: A temple completed in 1990 by Sri Prakash Narayan Punj on the road between Prayagraj and Varanasi, marking the spot where tradition holds Sita returned to the earth. Ram Navami is its principal festival.
story: Living at Valmiki's hermitage, Sita is said to have asked the earth to take her back after her sons Luv and Kush seized Rama's Ashvamedha horse and fought his army.

name: Shyam Kaka Temple
significance: Built in 1845 on the order of Queen Bhagali Devi in memory of her husband, the local ruler Shyam Dev Khinchi, with the chieftain Amara Singh Gurjar installed as first head priest. Damaged in the British period and rebuilt in August 1987, it is now a protected site of the Archaeological Survey of India.
story: A carved panel shows six Arab men at prayer: local lore says visiting Arabs questioned the priest about the sanctity of Mecca and Medina, and he showed them both cities within the temple, whereupon they prayed there.

name: Sekhareswar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Lathanga in Jagatsinghpur district run by a board of trustees, whose Varuni Yatra is described as a thousand years old. Local institutions including a Sanskrit college take their name from the shrine.

name: Kothandaramaswamy Temple
deity: Rama (Kothandaramaswamy), with Lakshmana, Sita, Hanuman and Vibhishana
significance: A Vaishnava shrine 13 km from Rameswaram, counted among the 108 Abhimana Kshethrams, and the only structure at Dhanushkodi left standing by the cyclone of 1964. A proposed alignment of the Sethusamudram canal was dropped because it would have required demolishing it.
story: This is held to be where Vibhishana, Ravana's brother, surrendered to Rama's army, and where Rama afterwards crowned him king of Lanka.

name: Baba Gangeshwarnath Dham
significance: A Shiva temple at Itahara Uparwar in Bhadohi district, built by Shiv Lal Singh with the help of the Kashi Naresh. It stands on a reach where the Ganges runs from west to east.

name: Kusacode Shri Mahadeva Temple
deity: Shiva, in the form of Kiratha Moorthi
significance: A Shiva temple near Thirumala classed as a Major temple by the Travancore Devaswom Board, with an eight-day Thrikkodiyettu festival. On Shivaratri it is among the busiest shrines in Thiruvananthapuram district after Sreekanteshwaram.

name: Sidhhanath Temple, Kharsundi
deity: Siddhanath (Nathbaba), held to be an incarnation of Shiva
significance: A hill shrine at Kharsundi in Sangli district, roughly four and a half centuries old, whose main gathering falls on Chaitra Ashtami. Nathbaba is a widely followed kuladaivat of the surrounding country.
story: Siddhanath is said to have two wives, Jogeshwari who lives at the temple and Zakabai near Neilkarnji, and by the first wife's condition he may visit the second only once in three years; the spring at Gohdapur is said to have opened where his horse struck the ground as he fled a snake set to stop the meeting.

name: Hulimavu Cave Temple
significance: A cave shrine cut into a single rock outcrop off Bannerghatta Road in south Bangalore, reckoned four to five centuries old and administered by the Sri Sri Bala Gangadaraswami Mutt. It holds three consecrated shrines and a meditation mantapa.
story: The saint Sri Ramanand Swamiji is said to have performed tapas in the cave for many years, and his samadhi lies inside it.

name: Shitala Mata Temple, Patna
deity: Shitala Mata, worshipped as a form of Durga
significance: A goddess temple in Patna City regarded as a Shakta pitha and a centre of Durga worship in the old quarter of the Bihar capital.

name: Shri Kalyan Temple, Diggi
significance: An old Vaishnava shrine at Diggi in Tonk district, rebuilt in 1527, and one of Rajasthan's larger pilgrimage centres. Devotees hold the water offered here to cure skin disease.
story: King Digva, struck with leprosy, is said to have recovered his health after recovering an image of Vishnu from the sea and installing it at Diggi, and the god was thereafter called Kalyanji, the benevolent one.

name: Shree Balaji Mandir
style: Built to shilpa, agama and vastu shastra
significance: A Venkateshwara temple at Charkop in Kandivali West that presents itself as the god's second home after Tirupati. Andal, the adopted daughter of Periyalwar, is honoured here through the Tiruppavai during Dhanurmas.

name: Ganpati Temple, Tasgaon
style: South Indian, with a seven-storeyed gopura
significance: Begun in 1779 by Parasuram Bhau Patwardhan, Sar-Senapati to the Peshwa, and finished by his son Appa Patwardhan in 1799, this temple is known for its 29 m gopura and for an idol whose trunk curves to the right. Its 30 ft chariot procession the day after Bhadrapada Chaturthi has run since 1785.

name: Sethu Kshetram
deity: Ganapathi, with a shrine to Ayyappan
significance: A Ganapati temple on the Mount-Poonamallee Road at Porur, founded in 1964 for the workforce of W. S. Industries and standing within the company campus. Its foundation stone was laid by the Shankaracharya of Sringeri.

name: Shiv Khori
deity: Shiva, as a naturally formed lingam
significance: A cave shrine about 200 m deep in Reasi district, some 80 km from Katra, whose rock formations are read as images of the gods around a self-formed lingam. Pilgrim numbers rose to roughly two million by 2016 after the Shiv Khori Shrine Board was set up in December 2003.
story: One passage inside the cave, now sealed, is said to have run through to the Amarnath cave in Kashmir.

name: Shri Vinayaka Shankaranarayana Durgamba Temple
significance: A three-deity temple on the bank of the Netravathi at Nandavara in Dakshina Kannada, with a sanctum, tirtha mantapa, welcome gopuram and brass-clad flagstaff. Alongside its Jathra Mahotsava it runs midday meals and free medical camps for the surrounding villages.

name: Serugudi Sukshmapureeswarar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Serugudi in Tiruvarur district counted among the Padal Petra Sthalams, its deity sung by the Nayanar saint Sambandar. The precinct also holds shrines to Ganesha, Murugan and the Navagrahas.

name: Semmeninathar Karumbeswarar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple near Vishnampettai in Thanjavur district, one of the Padal Petra Sthalams, praised in the hymns of Sambandar and Thirunavukkarasar. Tradition links its building to the Chola king Karikala.
story: Parasurama is said to have worshipped Shiva here to be freed of the sin of killing the Kshatriyas.

name: Shankaragaurishvara Temple, Pattan
significance: Raised by King Shankaravarman of the Utpala dynasty at Pattan, about 27 km from Srinagar, with deeply carved facades and pedimented entrance columns. It is now ruinous and no longer in worship, and stands beside the smaller Sugandhesha temple that Shankaravarman built for his queen.

name: Siddhanath Temple, Mhaswad
deity: Siddhanath, an incarnation of Shiva and kshetrapal of the region
significance: A Shaiva temple at Mhaswad in Satara district, about 56 km from Pandharpur, attributed to the Badami Chalukyas and completed on its second side in 1738 by their descendant Dubal of Karad. Its Mhaswad Yatra, with a chariot of Siddhanath and crowds smeared in pink gulal, draws devotees from across India.

name: Moteshwar Mahadev
place: Ujjanak, Kashipur, Udham Singh Nagar district
deity: Shiva, worshipped as Bhimashankar in an unusually large lingam
significance: A Shiva temple at Ujjanak near Kashipur named for the sheer girth of its lingam, which cannot be encircled by two hands. The complex also holds shrines of Bhairav Nath, the Shiv Ganga Kund and Maa Jagdamba Bhagwati Balsundari, and holds fairs at Maha Shivaratri, Chaitra and Shravan.
story: Local tradition holds that Dronacharya set Bhima to rebuilding the shrine, after which it came to be called Bheem Shankar.

name: Sharvani Devasthan
place: Salgaonwada, Adavalpal, near Bicholim, North Goa district
deity: Sharvani, with Vetoba (a form of Shiva)
significance: A Goan goddess temple at Salgaonwada near Bicholim, the kuladevata of the Salgaonkar, Prabhu, Naik, Shenoy, Dhond and Petkar families. Its original shrine stood at Saligaon before the deity was moved here.

name: Siruvapuri Sri Balasubrahmanyam Temple
significance: A Murugan temple in Thiruvallur district that temple records place more than five hundred years back. The 14th-century poet Arunagirinathar came here repeatedly and composed Thiruppugal verses on its deity.
story: Lava and Kusha, the sons of Rama, are said to have worshipped at this spot.

name: Paramekkavu Bagavathi Temple
significance: One of the largest Bhagavathi shrines of central Kerala and the head of the Paramekkavu side of the Thrissur Pooram, the division of the city's temples into two competing groups being the work of Sakthan Thampuran. Its devaswom also runs the Paramekkavu Vidya Mandir school.

name: Sri Nellikulangara Bhagavathi Temple
significance: The goddess temple of Nemmara in Palakkad district, whose Nenmara Vallanghi Vela in April is built on a friendly rivalry between the villages of Nemmara and Vallangi. The festival brings Kummattikali, Karivela and a parade of caparisoned elephants.

name: Chembukkavu Bhagavathy Temple
significance: A Thrissur city temple counted among the 108 Durga shrines of Kerala and a participant in the Thrissur Pooram, administered by the Cochin Devaswom Board. Its goddess is reckoned the younger sister of the Bhagavathi at Ayyanthole, and her processions to Vadakkumnathan are timed before the sun grows strong.

name: Pataleshwar Mandir
significance: A Shiva temple on Jadhua Road in Hajipur, Vaishali district, held locally to be of ancient standing and busiest at Shivratri.
story: The lingam here is said to have risen out of the ground of its own accord, making the shrine a swayambhu one.
